text.en: An incorporated noun-verb combination behaves phonologically as a single word, with the result that only a single accent is retained and the accent of the verb weakens or disappears, as illustrated by *turep-ta* ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--an-incorporated-noun-verb-combination-behaves-phonologically-as⟧.
text.ja: 名詞と動詞が抱合した表現は音韻的に一語として振る舞い、アクセントは一つだけ保たれ、動詞のアクセントは弱まるかなくなる。これは*turep-ta*に示される⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--an-incorporated-noun-verb-combination-behaves-phonologically-as⟧。

text.en: In compound words formed from two or more independent words, the general tendency is for only the accent of the initial element to be retained and for the whole compound to be treated as a single word, as seen in *kamúy* and *nomí* yielding *kamúynomi*, and *hórka* and *reyé* yielding *hórkareyep* ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-compound-words-formed-from-two-or-more⟧. When the initial element of a compound is monosyllabic, accent is placed on that initial element, as in *ni* and *tek* yielding *nítek* ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-the-initial-element-of-a-compound-word⟧. Secondary accents belonging to non-initial stems are deleted in compound words and noun-incorporation structures ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-compound-words-and-noun-incorporation-structures-secondary⟧. More generally, in morphosyntactically complex forms the primary accent falls on the first element and accent on subsequent elements is reduced, with the stem taking priority over derivational suffixes ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-morphosyntactically-complex-forms-the-general-rule-is⟧. When the first element is CVC and the second element is vowel-initial, however, accent is often assigned according to the iambic rule rather than the first-element priority rule ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-a-compound-has-a-cvc-initial-element⟧. A compound may also shift its accent to follow the iambic rule when it becomes lexicalized and speakers perceive it as monomorphemic ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--a-compound-shifts-its-accent-to-follow-the⟧.
text.ja: 2つ以上の自立語による複合語では、大ざっぱな傾向として前部要素のアクセントだけが残り、全体が1語として扱われる。これは*kamúy*と*nomí*から*kamúynomi*が、*hórka*と*reyé*から*hórkareyep*が形成される例に示される⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-compound-words-formed-from-two-or-more⟧。複合語の前部要素が単音節語である場合、*ni*と*tek*から*nítek*が形成されるように、前部要素にアクセントが置かれる⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-the-initial-element-of-a-compound-word⟧。複合語や名詞抱合構造において、主アクセント以外の語幹のアクセントは削除される⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-compound-words-and-noun-incorporation-structures-secondary⟧。より一般的に、形態統語的に複合的な形式では第1要素に主アクセントが置かれ後続要素のアクセントは弱められ、派生においては接尾辞よりも語幹が優先される⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-morphosyntactically-complex-forms-the-general-rule-is⟧。ただし、第1要素がCVCで第2要素が母音初頭である場合には、第1要素優先規則ではなく短長格規則に従ってアクセントが置かれることが多い⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-a-compound-has-a-cvc-initial-element⟧。また、複合語が語彙化し話者に単一形態素として意識されるようになると、アクセントが短長格規則に従う形へシフトすることがある⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--a-compound-shifts-its-accent-to-follow-the⟧。

text.en: When derivational prefixes attach, the prefixed form is treated as a single word and the general accent principles apply, which may shift the accent from the stem's original position, as illustrated by *iták* and *yáykoytak*, and *puní* and *epúni* ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-derivational-prefixes-attach-the-prefixed-form-is⟧.
text.ja: 派生接頭辞が付く場合には、接辞を含めた全体が1語とみなされて一般的なアクセント原則が適用されるため、元の語のアクセントが移動することがある。これは*iták*と*yáykoytak*、および*puní*と*epúni*に示される⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-derivational-prefixes-attach-the-prefixed-form-is⟧。

text.en: The archaic causative suffix *-V* shifts accent placement, whereas the productive causative suffix *-re*/*-e*/*-te* does not shift accent ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--causative-v-shifts-accent-unlike-productive-suffixes⟧. More specifically, the allomorphic causative suffix *-re*/*-e*/*-te* does not affect accentuation in Hokkaido/southwest Ainu ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--the-allomorphic-causative-suffix-re-e-te-does⟧. Suffixes generally do not affect accent position, but when causative suffixes *-re*, *-te*, or *-e* attach to monosyllabic verbs, the accent remains on the stem syllable, producing exceptions to Principle 2, as in *ére*, *kúre*, and *káre* ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--suffixes-usually-do-not-affect-accent-but-when⟧. When *-re* is suffixed to a monosyllabic verb stem to make it disyllabic, the accent position does not change, as in *e* 'eat' yielding *é-re* 'feed', whereas when *-e* is suffixed to an *r*-final stem to make it disyllabic, the accent shifts to the second syllable, as in *kór* 'have' yielding *koré* 'give' ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-re-is-suffixed-to-a-monosyllabic-verb⟧. In some lexicalized causatives, the suffix *-re*/*-e*/*-te* shifts accentuation in accordance with the accent rules, as in *kor* 'have' yielding *ko.r-e* 'make/let have, give' ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-some-lexicalized-causatives-the-causative-suffix-re⟧. Nakagawa 2024 asserts that in the causative verb *kore* 'give' derived from *kor* 'have', the accent is the regular *koré* rather than *kóre* because awareness of it as a derived form has weakened ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-the-causative-verb-kore-give-from-kor⟧. When a suffix or word-final element becomes fully lexicalized with the stem into a single unit, the accent shifts to the second syllable under rule (4), as in *kayé*, *tuyé*, and *hashínau* ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-a-suffix-or-word-final-element-becomes⟧.
text.ja: 古風な使役接尾辞*-V*はアクセントの移動を引き起こすが、生産的な使役接尾辞*-re*/*-e*/*-te*はアクセントを移動させない⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--causative-v-shifts-accent-unlike-productive-suffixes⟧。より具体的には、北海道・南西方言において使役接尾辞の異形態*-re*/*-e*/*-te*はアクセント付与に影響を与えない⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--the-allomorphic-causative-suffix-re-e-te-does⟧。接尾辞は通常アクセントの位置に影響を与えないが、単音節語に使役接尾辞*-re*、*-te*、*-e*が付いた場合にはアクセントが語幹に残り、原則2の例外となることがある。これは*ére*、*kúre*、*káre*に示される⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--suffixes-usually-do-not-affect-accent-but-when⟧。一音節の動詞語幹に*-re*が付いて二音節になってもアクセントの位置は変わらず（例：*e*「食べる」→*é-re*「食べさせる」）、r で終わる語幹に*-e*が付いて二音節になった場合はアクセントが第二音節に移動する（例：*kór*「持つ」→*koré*「持たせる」）⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-re-is-suffixed-to-a-monosyllabic-verb⟧。一部の語彙化された使役形において、接尾辞*-re*/*-e*/*-te*はアクセント規則に従ってアクセントの位置を変化させ、*kor*「持つ」から*ko.r-e*「持たせる、与える」が形成される⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-some-lexicalized-causatives-the-causative-suffix-re⟧。Nakagawa 2024は、*kor*「持つ」から派生した使役形*kore*「与える」では派生語としての語源意識が薄れたため*kóre*ではなく通常の原則2に従い*koré*となると主張する⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-the-causative-verb-kore-give-from-kor⟧。接尾辞や語尾が語幹と熟成して一単位と感じられるようになると、規則(4)の支配を受けて第2音節にアクセントが置かれるようになり、*kayé*、*tuyé*、*hashínau*がその例である⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-a-suffix-or-word-final-element-becomes⟧。

text.en: Most personal prefixes trigger relocation of the word accent ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--most-personal-prefixes-trigger-relocation-of-the-word⟧. The phonological alternations and accent shifts that occur when personal affixes attach to nouns are identical to those in transitive verb inflection: *ku-* and *e-* shift accent to the following syllable, whereas *eci-* and *a-* retain the original accent; before vowel-initial stems *ku-* becomes *k-* and *ci-* becomes *c-*, taking the accent ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--the-phonological-alternations-and-accent-shifts-that-occur⟧.
text.ja: 大部分の人称接頭辞はアクセントの位置の移動を引き起こす⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--most-personal-prefixes-trigger-relocation-of-the-word⟧。人称接辞が名詞に付く場合に起こる音の交替現象やアクセントの移動は他動詞の人称変化の場合と同じであり、*ku-*と*e-*は次の音節にアクセントを移動させ、*eci-*と*a-*は元のアクセント位置を保ち、母音の前で*ku-*は*k-*、*ci-*は*c-*となりその音節にアクセントが置かれる⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--the-phonological-alternations-and-accent-shifts-that-occur⟧。

text.en: The prefixes *ku-* '1sg.nom', *ci-* '1pl.excl.nom', and *e-* '2sg.nom' shift the accent of the verb to the immediately following syllable ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--the-prefixes-ku-1sg-nom-ci-1pl-excl⟧. When *ku=*, *e=*, or *ci=* attach to a word whose base had an open first syllable, the prefixed form is treated as a single word and Principle 2 causes the accent to shift one syllable leftward onto the base's original first syllable, as in *hopúni* yielding *ku=hópuni* and *nanú* yielding *e=nánu* ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-personal-prefixes-ku-e-or-ci-attach⟧. In Saru and Chitose dialects, *ku=* and *ci=* contract to *k=* and *c=* before stems beginning with *a*, *u*, *e*, or *o* after accent shift has occurred, resulting in surface accent on the fused initial syllable, as in *omáre* yielding *k=ómare* and *etú* yielding *c=étu* ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-saru-and-chitose-dialects-ku-and-ci⟧. In those same dialects, when *ku=* or *e=* precedes an open initial syllable beginning with *i-*, vowel weakening turns *i* into the coda glide *y* of the first syllable, so that *ku=i-* becomes *kuy-* and *e=i-* becomes *ey-*, placing the accent on the first syllable, as in *ipe* yielding *kúype* and *itak* yielding *éytak* ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-saru-and-chitose-dialects-when-ku-or⟧. Before stems starting with *i* whose first syllable is closed, however, the *i* → *y* weakening after *ku=* or *e=* does not occur because it would create an impossible CCC cluster, resulting in forms such as *kuínkar* and *kuíkka* ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--before-stems-starting-with-i-whose-first-syllable⟧. Attaching *ku=* to the verb *mokór* causes the pitch accent to shift to the prefix, producing *ku mókor* ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--attaching-the-1st-person-prefix-ku-to-the⟧.
text.ja: *ku-*「私が」、*ci-*「私達（除外的）が」、*e-*「お前が」はアクセントをその次の音節に移動させる⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--the-prefixes-ku-1sg-nom-ci-1pl-excl⟧。*ku=*、*e=*、*ci=*が前接する場合、全体が1語とみなされ、元の語の第1音節が開音節であれば原則2が適用されてアクセントが1音節前に移動する。これは*hopúni*から*ku=hópuni*が、*nanú*から*e=nánu*が形成される例に示される⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-personal-prefixes-ku-e-or-ci-attach⟧。沙流・千歳方言では、*a*、*u*、*e*、*o*で始まる語の前で*ku=*→*k=*、*ci=*→*c=*と母音が縮約し、アクセント移動後に適用されるため結果的にアクセントは第1音節に置かれる。これは*omáre*から*k=ómare*が、*etú*から*c=étu*が形成される例に示される⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-saru-and-chitose-dialects-ku-and-ci⟧。同じ方言では、*i*で始まり第1音節が開音節の語の前に*ku=*、*e=*がつくと母音弱化により*ku=i-*→*kuy-*、*e=i-*→*ey-*となり、アクセントは第1音節に置かれる。これは*ipe*から*kúype*が、*itak*から*éytak*が形成される例に示される⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--in-saru-and-chitose-dialects-when-ku-or⟧。ただし、*i*で始まっていても第1音節が閉音節である語の前では、子音が3つ連続する音節構造を避けるため*i*→*y*の交替は起こらず、*kuínkar*や*kuíkka*のようになる⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--before-stems-starting-with-i-whose-first-syllable⟧。動詞*mokór*に*ku=*が付くとアクセントが接辞側に移動し、*ku mókor*となる⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--attaching-the-1st-person-prefix-ku-to-the⟧。

text.en: The personal prefixes *a-* and *eci-* do not alter the accent placement of the stem to which they attach ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--non-shifting-prefixes-retain-stem-accent⟧. Bugaeva 2022 further asserts that the inflectional person prefix *a-* does not affect accent placement at all and can be analyzed as extrametrical ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--the-inflectional-person-prefix-a-does-not-affect⟧.
text.ja: 人称接頭辞*a-*および*eci-*は、接続する語幹のアクセント位置を変化させず維持する⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--non-shifting-prefixes-retain-stem-accent⟧。Bugaeva 2022はさらに、屈折接頭辞*a-*はアクセント配置に全く影響を与えず、外延的（extrametrical）であるとみなすことができると主張する⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--the-inflectional-person-prefix-a-does-not-affect⟧。

text.en: Personal suffixes such as *-as* and *-an* carry a secondary accent alongside the accent located on the verb stem ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--personal-suffixes-carry-a-secondary-accent-alongside-the⟧. This secondary accent on a personal suffix is lost when the verb stem is monosyllabic of the shape (C)VC ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--the-secondary-accent-on-a-personal-suffix-is⟧.
text.ja: 人称接尾辞*-as*や*-an*は、語幹上のアクセントと並んで副アクセントを帯びる⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--personal-suffixes-carry-a-secondary-accent-alongside-the⟧。ただし、語幹が(C)VC音節からなる場合、人称接尾辞上の副アクセントは消失する⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--the-secondary-accent-on-a-personal-suffix-is⟧。

text.en: When a closed monosyllabic noun takes the affiliative suffix, accent shifts to the second syllable, as in *shik* yielding *shikíhi*, *mat* yielding *machíhi*, and *kap* yielding *kapúhu*, whereas an open monosyllabic noun keeps the accent on the first syllable, as in *pa* yielding *páha*, *ko* yielding *kóho*, and *re* yielding *réhe* ⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-a-closed-monosyllabic-noun-takes-the-affiliative⟧.
text.ja: 閉音節の単音節名詞が所属形をとる場合は第2音節にアクセントが移り（*shik*→*shikíhi*、*mat*→*machíhi*、*kap*→*kapúhu*）、開音節の単音節名詞ではアクセントは第1音節にとどまる（*pa*→*páha*、*ko*→*kóho*、*re*→*réhe*）⟦claim:prosody/accent-in-compounds-and-affixation--when-a-closed-monosyllabic-noun-takes-the-affiliative⟧。
